sentences.text: Vectiraptor is a dromaeosaurid dinosaur genus from the Barremian stage of the United Kingdom.
The estimated body length of this animal was between 2.5 and 3 meters.
Fragmentary fossils reveal unique dromaeosaurid features such as short massive vertebrae, tall neural spines, and rib facets on long stalks.
One unique trait is an extra ridge subdividing the deep triangular depression on the underside of the side process in the front dorsal vertebrae.
The vertebrae featured extensive pneumatization with large camellate air spaces connected to respiratory air sacs.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — represents an adult individual estimated to be twenty to thirty years old based on bone growth lines.
Amateur paleontologist Mick Green discovered Vectiraptor in 2004 at Compton Bay on the Isle of Wight.
Nicholas Longrich, David Michael Martill, and Megan Jacobs named Vectiraptor greeni in 2021.
The genus name Vectiraptor means "Isle of Wight thief" in Latin.
The species name greeni honors Mick Green, the discoverer of the type material.
Features like large size, short dorsals, and specific neural spine characteristics suggest Vectiraptor is a member or relative of Eudromaeosauria.
Vectiraptor lived during the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
